# R7 capacity corpus

`cases.json` is the complete authored input inventory for `verify-r7-capacity.sh`. The fixture rejects missing, duplicated, reordered or modified cases. Inputs are deterministic synthetic repository data and fake provider responses; no provider credentials or external calls are used.

The default case supplies no limit override and completes 63 turns of seven read-only calls followed by `finish_review`: 64 model calls and 442 charged tools. The configured case selects the supported 128-call authority and completes 127 turns of three read-only calls followed by `finish_review`: 128 model calls and 382 charged tools. Both construct 320 changed files with 64 added lines: one short canary line followed by 63 lines of 512 UTF-8 bytes. File bytes exactly match their diff. The tools paginate the entire changed-file inventory, read a diff, and read the short first line through production snapshot tools. The gate binds configured authority to the existing `TrustedConfiguredCallsReachRealProviderAndBothSessionConsumers` production configuration regression; the AOT fixture executes the effective 128-call authority, without claiming another configuration parser implementation.

Each following case launches a different process with a cleared environment. Successful children build a production SESSION and prepare/accept encrypted local state. Fresh children restore it, compare the complete plaintext digest and check the actual provider request against authored prior assistant reasoning, tool-call IDs, arguments, tool-result associations and untrusted user/tool roles. IPC contains only bounded metadata, a synthetic key and accepted lineage; it never contains a SESSION or repeated raw requests. Keys and repository canaries never appear in public reports.

The default predecessor then faces decoded-content capacity, conservative context, known output-token, response-body and monotonic deadline failures. Each failure must remain incomplete, reject SESSION construction and preserve the entire stored state inventory and exact accepted predecessor. Separate negatives mutate a large history's user role and tool-result call association at production SESSION admission, or restore selected current state with wrong policy/session scope. They must reject without bootstrap or a write. Explicit reset invokes the production reset operation before a fresh session and subsequent fresh-process continuation.

The separate Host proof runs the same failure stimuli through production ActionHost composition with synthetic GitHub/artifact ports. It checks canonical nonzero completion, absent success summary fields, `NotCommitted`, no candidate or publishing mutation, preserved accepted state and production reset. Protected candidate/acceptance/lineage ciphertext remains byte-identical; authenticated prior publication recovery control records may be cleaned by the existing Host recovery prelude. A store hook rejects any protected object upload during failures, including a transient candidate that could later be deleted. It is an in-process Host proof; the large local-state history chain is the fresh-process proof. Neither topology is a released-payload or paid-provider qualification.

The verifier requires all 15 child cases and eight Host cases and checks exact semantic observations. Framework/AOT parity retains counts, diagnostics, bounds and restore/reset/role observations while excluding observed elapsed time, allocation, process memory, process identity and randomized encrypted storage size. Refer to [the evidence report](../../../../../../docs/90_roadmap/r7-capacity-evidence.md) for measured workload sizes, limits and bottlenecks.
